title: Localization of the prime-to-ell alteration site at an alteration object
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\ell$ be a prime. Let $T\to S$ be an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, with the category and topology of $\ell^{\prime}$-alterations defined in [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Thus $T$ is reduced and finite type over $S$, and its generic points map to generic points of $S$ with finite residue-field extensions. The slice category $(\operatorname{alt}/S)/T$ has as objects morphisms $X\to T$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$, and as morphisms the commuting triangles over $T$. Composition with $T\to S$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{alt}/T\simeq(\operatorname{alt}/S)/T$, acting as the identity on the underlying schemes and their maps over $T$. Under this equivalence the topology of $\ell^{\prime}$-alterations on $\operatorname{alt}/T$ equals the localized topology of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ [def-weil-pbc-topos]: a sieve on an object $X\to T$ is covering in the localized topology exactly when its underlying sieve on $X$ is covering in $\operatorname{alt}/S$. In particular, for every set-indexed family of objects $X_a\to T$ of $\operatorname{alt}/T$, the family is covering in $\operatorname{alt}/T$ if and only if its corresponding family of arrows to $T$ is covering in $\operatorname{alt}/S$.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.1.10, 1.2.3 and proof of Proposition 1.2.6, printed pp.24--25 (the alteration category over an object); Definitions 2.1.1--2.1.2 and 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.2, printed pp.26--28 (intrinsic, base-change-stable generators). The localization of a generated topology is Mathlib CategoryTheory.over_toGrothendieck_eq_toGrothendieck_comap_forget, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Over.lean lines 540--548; the scheme-category equivalence is an additional assertion, so this is not a Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $T$ is Noetherian, so $\operatorname{alt}/T$ is defined. For $X\to T$ in this category, composition with $T\to S$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its source is still reduced; each generic point maps first to a generic point of $T$ and then one of $S$. The two finite residue extensions compose to a finite extension: products of finite vector-space spanning sets span the tower. Thus the composite is in $\operatorname{alt}/S$ by [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. This defines the functor in the statement on objects, and it leaves every map unchanged.

source.place: II Definition 1.2.2 and proof of Proposition 1.2.6, printed p.25: composition of maximally finite dominant finite-type morphisms.

proof.text: Conversely, let $u:X\to T$ be an object of $(\operatorname{alt}/S)/T$. Apply [lem-per-alteration-arrow-properties] to its underlying arrow: $u$ is finite type, maximally dominant, and has finite generic residue extensions. Its source is reduced, so it is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/T$ by [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. A morphism in either category is exactly a scheme map over $T$. Hence this assignment is an inverse functor: the composites preserve each scheme and map and its given structure arrow. This proves the categorical equivalence, including full faithfulness.

source.place: II Proposition 1.1.10, 1.2.3 and the first paragraph of the proof of 1.2.6, printed pp.24--25.

proof.text: Let $K_S$ and $K_T$ denote the two raw generating precoverages of [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Under the preceding equivalence, $K_T$ is precisely the inverse image of $K_S$ under the slice forgetful functor. Indeed, on any family with target $Y\to T$, its underlying schemes, maps, points and residue-field homomorphisms are identical. Etaleness and the existence of a residue-degree-prime-to-$\ell$ lift at every point are therefore unchanged. For a singleton, properness, surjectivity and the generic-point residue-degree conditions are likewise unchanged. Every possible source over $Y$ occurs on both sides by Steps 1--2, so this is equality of generating presieves, not merely one inclusion.

source.place: II Definitions 2.1.1 and 2.3.1, printed pp.26,28; the conditions are intrinsic to the arrows.

proof.text: The raw precoverage $K_S$ has pullbacks and is stable under base change by [lem-per-alteration-generators-pullback]. Apply [lem-per-generated-topology-slice] with $\mathcal C=\operatorname{alt}/S$ and object $T$. Its hypotheses are exactly these two properties; no composition stability of the raw generators is needed. The topology on $\operatorname{alt}/S$ is $J_{K_S}$ by its definition [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Step 3 identifies the precoverage in the slice with $K_T$, so the equality $J_{K_S}|_T=J_{K_T}$ proves the required equality of topologies under Step 2's equivalence.

source.place: II Remark 2.3.2, printed p.28; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Over.lean:541--548 for localization of a generated topology.

proof.text: For a sieve on $Y\to T$, forgetting the maps to $T$ gives a sieve on $Y$: every arrow $Z\to Y$ has the unique structure map $Z\to Y\to T$, and every further precomposition has this same forced structure. This is the sieve correspondence in [lem-per-generated-topology-slice]. Its covering criterion and Step 4 give the stated criterion for arbitrary sieves. The sieve generated by a family corresponds to the sieve generated by its underlying arrows, since a factorization through a family member over $Y$ automatically commutes with the forced maps to $T$. Apply this at the object $1_T:T\to T$ to obtain the last assertion for every set-indexed family, including the empty family.

source.place: II 2.3.1, printed p.28; generated sieves and the explicit slice sieve correspondence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_alterationSiteLocalization (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S] (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (T : Alt S) : ∃ (hT : IsNoetherian T.obj.left), ∃ (e : @Alt T.obj.left hT ≌ Over T), e.functor ⋙ Over.post (ObjectProperty.ι _) ⋙ T.obj.iteratedSliceForward = ObjectProperty.ι _ ∧ (∀ (X : @Alt T.obj.left hT) (R : Sieve (e.functor.obj X)), R.functorPullback e.functor ∈ @topology T.obj.left hT ell inferInstance X ↔ R ∈ (topology S ell).over T (e.functor.obj X)) ∧ (∀ (Y : Over T) (R : Sieve Y), R ∈ (topology S ell).over T Y ↔ Sieve.overEquiv Y R ∈ topology S ell Y.left) ∧ (∀ (I : Type w) (U : I → Over T), Sieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ e.inverse.obj (U i)) (fun i ↦ e.inverse.map (Over.homMk (U i).hom : U i ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 T))) ∈ @topology T.obj.left hT ell inferInstance (e.inverse.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 T))) ↔ IsCoveringFamily ell (fun i ↦ (U i).left) (fun i ↦ (U i).hom))
